subject: Order Form & GDPR: cross-border transfer impact and implementation path
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@novamed.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form redlines + SCCs questions

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached are our redlines to the order form; legal also flagged GDPR/SCCs concerns and asked for clarity on how Redwood intends to comply with cross-border transfer obligations. Two specific asks from our side: 1) confirmation on the SCCs you propose to incorporate (old 2010, 2021, or derogations), and 2) whether Redwood can provide a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) or equivalent technical/organizational evidence (data localization options, encryption at rest details).

We need this answered before procurement will move to signature. Can you please route to your privacy/legal team and advise an implementation timeline?

Attachments: Novamed_OrderForm_Redlines_20260513.docx (docx)

Best,
Sarah Lim
Head of Vendor Risk — Novamed Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@novamed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redlines + SCCs questions

Hi Sarah — thank you for sending the redlines and the matrix. I’ve looped in Karthik (privacy) and Laura (legal) to review the SCCs questions and the Order Form redlines. High-level response below and next steps: 

- We can incorporate the new EU SCCs (2021) by reference in the MSA/Order Form; our standard DPA references the 2021 SCCs for processor transfers.
- We maintain optional region routing (EU-only) on Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted customers we offer contractual commitments plus operational controls. Technical evidence (encryption-at-rest, key management) can be provided as part of a TIA/evidence bundle.

Next steps / ask of Novamed: please confirm whether the preferred model is (A) EU-only Dedicated pool, (B) Hosted with contractual SCCs + evidence bundle, or (C) hybrid. That will determine the implementation timeline and any additional order form language.

Target timeline: internal review by EOD Monday (we’ll try to be faster), proposed redline back to you by Wednesday. If you need a faster SLA, flag below and we’ll escalate.

Attachments: SCCs_Comparison_Matrix.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy & Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@novamed.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 08:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redlines + SCCs questions

Neha / Karthik — I reviewed Novamed’s redlines and Sarah’s notes. Key points and proposed approach below: 

1) SCCs/version: we will propose the 2021 SCCs in our redline (processor-to-controller and controller-to-processor where applicable). Ask Novamed to confirm whether they require insertion of the SCCs text into the DPA or are comfortable with incorporation by reference plus a signed addendum.

2) Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): recommend we offer a short TIA attachment to the DPA that documents our transfer risk analysis, encryption/KMS controls, subprocessors list and geolocation routing options. This should satisfy most vendor-risk teams.

3) Order Form language: recommend a new optional Order Form toggle clause for "EU-only routing" (for Dedicated/Private). For Hosted, we propose explicit fallback language: if EU-only routing cannot be guaranteed, Redwood will provide contractual commitments + documented mitigation (TIA) and right-to-audit windows.

4) Redline suggestions: I will prepare a marked-up DPA (tracked changes) removing vendor-favorable escape language in the current redlines (notably section 4.2 on subcontractor liability) and insert the TIA reference and a carveout list for critical subprocessors.

5) Timeline / escalation: I'll send the legal redline back by Wednesday EOD. If Novamed needs signature sooner, we should consider a short-term addendum agreeing to an interim evidence package with a 30-day implementation milestone. Ben — can you confirm whether there's leverage on procurement timeline (discount window / PO date) that would justify escalation?

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Legal
---

From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@novamed.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Novamed Procurement <procurement@novamed.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2026 15:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redlines + SCCs questions

Laura / Neha — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed plan. Novamed’s legal team prefers: 

- Incorporation of the 2021 SCCs by reference + a signed Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) that includes our standard attestations.
- For commercial terms, we’ll accept an interim evidence package for Hosted (contracted SCCs + evidence) provided that the final TIA and KMS details are delivered within 30 calendar days post-signature.
- We will also request an explicit Order Form checkbox for EU-only routing; if the option is selected we’ll expect confirmation of dedicated pool allocation and SLA language for data locality.

Next: we’ll wait for Laura’s redline. Procurement has a soft PO window open until the end of next week — if Redwood can commit to the 30-day evidence delivery and the TIA template by Wednesday, we can clear legal and push to signature.

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of Vendor Risk — Novamed Health
